basis: Defined by dysfunction of basal ganglia motor pathways; rigidity and tremor do not establish primary muscle damage.
Bile duct paucity, intellectual disability and ear canal atresia define the syndrome; VSD frequent (30-79%). Clubfeet omitted because of the cap.
Isolated hereditary hypotrichosis; sparse scalp and body hair in 4/4 patients.
Defined by intellectual developmental impairment, language impairment and dystonia-parkinsonism.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with neuropathy; optic atrophy 3/8, cardiomyopathy 3/8 and lower-limb amyotrophy frequent (30-79%). Elevated lactate alone adds no metabolic axis.
Congenital malformation of the urethral opening; the renal axis includes the urethra. Associated endocrine and other organ defects are occasional.
Cutaneous mucinosis denotes mucin deposition in the skin; no evidence establishes common systemic organ damage.
Hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy; distal muscle wasting and fixed foot deformities affect most patients.
Immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis. Purpura and arthralgia alone do not establish lasting skin or joint damage; renal and nerve involvement are not established at ≥30% for type III.
Immune-mediated inflammatory optic neuropathy causing visual dysfunction; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis. Other neurologic disease is excluded by definition.
Sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma arises predominantly in bladder or upper urinary tract; all listed site-specific children fall within the renal axis.
Benign neoplasm originating in mandibular bone; its location near the mouth does not establish gastrointestinal involvement.
Genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; scoliosis reported in 1/3 patients supports skeletal involvement at the threshold. Spaced teeth alone do not establish oral damage.
OTOA-related nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss.
Defined by developmental impairment and epilepsy. Vascular defects are isolated reports; constipation in 11/14 does not establish direct intestinal injury.
Localized nodular lesion arising from gingiva; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Inherited respiratory ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis in 9/12; recurrent middle-ear inflammation in 8/12 supports otologic involvement.
Metabolic liver disease with neurodegeneration; ichthyosis/dermatitis 4/6. Gingival overgrowth 3/6, hearing loss 2/6 and contractures 2/6 omitted by cap; cortical blindness is neurologic.
Defined by immune-mediated hypersensitivity to a drug; no particular organ sustains direct lasting damage across most cases.
Congenital external-ear malformation, commonly with canal atresia and conductive hearing loss. Secondary speech delay does not establish neurologic damage.
Androgen resistance is an endocrine disorder; urethral malformation from hypospadias is frequent (30-79%; perineal hypospadias 5/5). Reproductive and breast findings have no axis.
Phenytoin poisoning primarily causes CNS toxicity, including cerebellar dysfunction and impaired consciousness; other organ injuries are not consistently common.
Carcinoma originating in uterine endometrium, a reproductive organ outside the axes; no common direct involvement of another organ is specified.
Immune-mediated crescentic glomerular inflammation with rapid renal function loss; systemic manifestations depend on the underlying disease.
Benign cartilage neoplasm involving a phalanx; localized skeletal disease.
